prompt:
GAME ITEM SPRITE. One single object seen from directly above, centred, like an item lying on the ground in a top-down strategy game.

Create an ORIGINAL game item sprite for a radio amateur's QSL card: a single stiff postcard that confirms a radio contact. Image 1 is our approved radio item from the same game: match its outline weight, shading, palette and finish only. Do NOT copy its shape.

Draw ONLY the card, alone on a plain pure white background, lying flat and straight, filling about 70 percent of the canvas width. Square canvas.

A landscape-shaped card with a slightly worn cream border; its face shows a small painted landscape (a ridge of hills under a pale sky and a tiny radio mast on the ridge); a bold dark band across the top where a station's callsign would go, left plain; a small square stamp-like box in one corner, left plain.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around the card, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per area, muted warm colours, a few small clean details, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, logos, people or animals. No shadow outside the card.

prompt:
STRAIGHT FRONT VIEW, looking directly at a board hung on a wall, flat on, as a game draws a picture on a wall. No angle, no tilt, no perspective.

Create an ORIGINAL game building sprite for a wooden display board that holds postcards, as a radio amateur pins up the cards from stations they have contacted. Image 1 is our approved radio desk from the same game: match its outline weight, shading, palette and finish only. Do NOT copy its shape.

Landscape canvas. The board fills about 85 percent of the canvas width, centred, on a plain pure white background.

A dark varnished wooden frame around a cork board; on the cork, six EMPTY postcard-sized slots in two rows of three, each marked only by four small brass corner clips, the cork showing through: the cards are added separately. A small brass plate centred on the frame's bottom edge, left plain.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around every shape, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per material, muted warm wood, cork and brass colours, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, logos, people, cards or pictures in the slots. No shadow outside the board.

prompt:
STRAIGHT FRONT VIEW, looking directly at a framed certificate hung on a wall, flat on. No angle, no tilt, no perspective.

Create an ORIGINAL game building sprite for a framed radio award certificate, of the kind radio amateurs hang above their station. Image 1 is our approved radio desk from the same game: match its outline weight, shading, palette and finish only. Do NOT copy its shape.

Square canvas. The frame fills about 80 percent of the canvas, centred, on a plain pure white background.

A polished dark wooden frame with a thin gold inner edge around a cream certificate; on the certificate a decorative border, a small drawing of a globe with curved radio waves around it at the top, an empty band across the middle where words would go, and a red wax seal with a ribbon at the bottom corner.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around every shape, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per material, muted warm colours with the gold and red seal, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, logos or people. No shadow outside the frame.
